title: Manager Corporate Finance
description:
Position: Manager Corporate Finance
Purpose (Strategic
KPIs):
To assist the Chief Finance Officer in investment matters, financial
projections and modeling
Responsibilities
Financial planning
The finance manager will prepare a detailed financial plan in order to
develop the effective Financial systems and practices.
Budgetary Management
Making internal budgetary schemes and recommending strategies for the
better overall budgetary management is a responsibility on part of the
Manager Finance.
Financial Evaluation
After having the technical approval of the proposal, Manager Finance has
the responsibility to evaluate the financial proposal as an internal
evaluator in accordance with the evaluation criteria defined by the R&D
Fund Company.
Pre-approval negotiations
Manager Finance has the responsibility to negotiate with the Principal
Investigator on the financial grounds of the project proposal including
requires & proposed funds and other allied matters.
Investment Strategies
Manager Finance is responsible for recommending the investment
strategies for the residual funds of the Ignite Company
Fund Raising
Manager Finance has the responsibility to coordinate efforts to raise
funds through complementary sources nationally and internationally.
Provision of assistance and advice
The position is responsible to prove assistance and advice to the CFO in
all financial matters/activities of the R&D Fund Company.
Project Recommendation
Forwarding Recommendations and preparing penetrations for the, CFO,
CEO, Board and F&A Committee regarding the evaluated/ approved
projects.
The incumbent should be an MBA (finance) / CFA
Qualification
Experience:
&
Should have at least 7-10 years relevant experience preferably in a
financial institution
Knowledge
&
Skills
Should have an understanding of contemporary investment practices
domestically and internationally
Reports To:
CFO
Remuneration/
Benefits:
Contract basis, market competitive salary, car monetization, medical and
other facilities.

qualifications: Association of Chartered Certified Accountants (ACCA UK)
description:
Position: Assistant Manager Financial Accounting
Key Responsibilities

The role of Assistant Manager Financial Accounting is to assist the

reconciliations, book-keeping, management reporting etc.

daily basis.
Responsible for daily transactions and book keeping.
Ensure timely payments to implementing partners & vendors.
To support compliance with mandatory requirements of the
Government of Pakistan, as applicable.
To maintain proper auditable documentation for ensuring
compliance to the required policies.
Deposit taxes being deducted on staff salaries, payments for
goods and services in accordance with income tax laws.
Deposit GST being withheld on purchase of goods and services
in accordance with sales tax laws in timely manner.
Timely preparation of quarterly and annual WHT statements
as per Income Tax Ordinance 2001.
Timely preparation of monthly WHT statements of Sales Tax.
Provide documentation required by auditors in timely manner.
Coordination with Accountant General of Pakistan Revenues,
banks, tax consultant, external auditor & internal auditor.
To support supervisor on any/all assigned tasks

and Abilities
Analysis of Financial Statements and Financial Modelling
Time Management
MS-Office (specially Word, Excel and Access).
Strong Presentation Skills.
Strong Critical and Analytical Thinking.
A self-starter that can work under pressure with minimum
supervision.
Effective writing skills

Experience:
Remuneration/

&
CA-Intermediate / Certificate in Accounting & Finance
(CAF) with completed articleship from a reputable
Chartered Accountants firm.
ACCA or ACMA with 3 years of relevant work experience.
Bachelors in Accounting with 3-5 years of relevant work
experience.
Contract basis, market competitive salary, with medical and other
facilities

title: Assistant Manager Collaboration
description:
Position: Assistant Manager Collaboration
Key
Responsibilities
(Strategic KPIs)
The Assistant Manager Collaboration will support the development,
execution, and management of strategic collaborations and partnerships
for Ignite’s initiatives. The role involves working closely with internal
teams and external stakeholders to advance program goals, promote
international cooperation, and strengthen the innovation ecosystem
Job Duties and
Responsibilities
Assist in identifying and pursuing partnership and collaboration
opportunities with local and international stakeholders.
Support the drafting and negotiation of partnership proposals, MoUs,
and agreements.
Coordinate partnership activities and facilitate communication
between Ignite and partner organizations.
Organize and represent Ignite at collaboration meetings, innovation
forums, and international delegations.
Support the implementation of joint initiatives, ensuring alignment
with project objectives and timelines.
Maintain and update partnership databases, track partnership KPIs,
and prepare periodic performance reports.
Contribute to planning, organizing, and managing events, workshops,
and networking sessions.
Research global best practices and recommend models for effective
collaboration in innovation and startup ecosystems.
Provide administrative and logistical support for collaboration
initiatives and international outreach activities.
Qualification &
Experience:
LLB (Mercantile law), BBA, Bachelors in Accounting & Finance,
Bachelors in Economics or Bachelors in International Relations.
At least 3 to 5 years of relevant professional experience in partnership
development, project coordination, public-private collaborations, or a
related field.
Knowledge &
Skills
Strong interpersonal, communication, and coordination skills.
Understanding of innovation ecosystems, entrepreneurship, and
digital economy sectors.
Ability to develop and manage relationships with diverse
stakeholders.
Good project management and organizational skills.
Proficiency in preparing reports, concept notes, and partnership
proposals.
Ability to work under pressure and manage multiple priorities
simultaneously.
Familiarity with national and international startup support
mechanisms will be an advantage.

Federal Government ministries, divisions, and departments.

engineering discipline.

Lead in overall planning, execution, and governance of the FCERT

employer: National Telecommunication and Information Security Board (NTISB)

Ensure proper documentation, reporting, and dissemination of incident reports, advisories, and alerts to higher authorities. • Prepare periodic performance, incident, and situational reports for submission to senior management and the competent authority

Integrating external threat intelligence feeds to stay ahead of emerging attack patterns and "zero-day" exploits.

description:

title: Public Finance Management Specialist (SPPS-II)
qualifications: Pakistan Institute of Public Finance Accountants-PIPFA
Master of International and Development Economics (MIDEC)
MBA Finance and Supply Chain Management
Master of Business and Information Technology (Finance)
Ms Statistics and Data Analytical Science
MSc International Economics Banking and Finance
description:
Undertake forecasting of revenues and expenditures on periodic basis, including annual, half-yearly and quarterly forecasts.
Provide technical assistance in the compilation, analysis and reporting of fiscal data for international credit rating agencies.
Conduct analysis of budgets and expenditures of sectors, Divisions, key Attached Departments and Autonomous Bodies.
Provide technical assistance in the detailed analysis and preparation of indicative budget ceilings for running of civil government, defence, pensions, grants, subsidies, net lending and the PSDP.
Prepare and maintain fiscal data spreadsheets in accordance with national and international standards.
Support the modernization of budgetary practices to enhance efficiency and optimize the utilization of public resources.
Undertake reforms in the budget preparation process through improvement of budgetary practices.
Strengthen budget execution and expenditure controls through monthly and quarterly reviews.
Review and update the Budget Manual in line with the requirements of the Public Finance Management Act and facilitate CFAOs in implementing the revised provisions of the Manual.
Devise and roll out initiatives to promote budget transparency, including fiscal risk disclosures, budget strategy paper, mid-year review report, fiscal policy statement, medium term performance-based budget, year-end performance monitoring report.
Support PAOs in implementing mid-year budget reporting, performance reporting against Output-Based Budgeting, reporting of budgeted and actual expenditure by output, and assessment of performance against targets.
Work closely with CFAOs and PAOs in Ministries and Divisions to mainstream the use of Output-Based Budgeting/Performance Budgeting and institutionalize the requirements of performance-based budgeting.
Devise and implement mechanisms to ensure efficient utilization of grants as part of the budget process.
Provide training and capacity-building support to budget officials of Ministries/Divisions as and when required.
Perform any other duties assigned by the Additional Finance Secretary Budget.
Education Qualification
Masters degree or higher in Finance, Economics, Accounting, Statistics or equivalent from a recognized university.
Experience Requirement
At least 10 years of relevant experience in public finance management, fiscal management, revenue management, budget allocation, public financial planning and budgeting.
Strong understanding of the PFM landscape in Pakistan, including donor-funded programmes and related reforms.
Demonstrated ability to effectively liaise and coordinate with key stakeholders.
Excellent written and oral communication skills.
Proficiency in the use of computers and office software packages MS Office, with advanced knowledge of spreadsheet and database applications, as well as experience in handling web-based management systems.

title: DIRECTOR GENERAL TELECOM WIRELESS
employer: Ministry of Information Technology and Telecommunication (MOITT)
description:
JOB SPECIFICATION:
EDUCATIONAL QUALIFICATION & EXPERIENCE:
Ph.D. in Electrical / Electronics / Computer Systems / Telecommunication Engineering
/ Engineering Management or related Engineering discipline from an HEC recognized local / foreign university with 05-years professional experience in the relevant field.
OR
Masters in Electrical / Electronics / Computer Systems/ Telecommunication Engineering / Engineering Management or related Engineering discipline from an HEC recognized local/foreign university with 07-year professional experience in the relevant field.
PROFESSIONAL CREDENTIALS:
The candidate must have following professional credentials:
Comprehensive understanding of modern telecommunication technologies, including next generation mobile networks, broadband, satellite communications, fixed-mobile convergence, RF communications & emerging wireless technologies, and related infrastructure requirements.
Strong knowledge of spectrum management, telecom policy, regulatory frameworks, market dynamics, licensing issues, quality of service, and the operational and commercial realities of the telecommunications sector.
Demonstrated experience in formulating, reviewing, and implementing ICT and telecom policies, strategies, frameworks, or regulatory interventions aimed at sector growth, investment facilitation, digital inclusion, and improved service delivery.
Proven ability to provide evidence-based technical, policy, and techno-economic advice to senior government forums, regulatory bodies, public sector entities, and other stakeholders.
Practical understanding of international telecommunications frameworks, including the work of the International Telecommunication Union and other relevant regional or international forums, with the ability to represent Pakistan effectively at national and international levels.
Proven leadership experience in managing professional teams, promoting a collaborative work culture, building institutional capacity, and ensuring timely delivery of assigned responsibilities.
Strong stakeholder engagement and interpersonal skills, including the ability to work effectively with government entities, regulators, telecom operators, industry associations, development partners, and international organizations.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to prepare policy briefs, analytical notes, consultation papers, presentations, speeches, and official positions on complex telecom and ICT matters.
Ability to perform effectively in a senior management position, including handling pressure, managing multiple priorities, coordinating across institutions, and ensuring continuous follow-up on critical matters.
Strong leadership, integrity, judgment, teamwork, and problem-solving skills, with a clear orientation toward public interest, sector development, and accountable decision-making.
Strong understanding of global telecommunications indices, rankings, and benchmarking methodologies, enabling the development of evidence-based policy recommendations and sector reform strategies.
Strong understanding of public sector procurement procedures, bidding processes as per government rules.
AGE LIMIT:
Maximum 62 years (to be calculated as on the closing date for submission of applications)
JOB DESCRIPTION/DELIVERABLE TASKS/TIMELINE:
Sr. No. Deliverable Tasks
Develop and organize progressive policy documents relating to telecom sector esp. wireless communication including, spectrum management, broadband, satellite communications and emerging technologies in alignment with MoITT vision of digital nation Pakistan.
Carryout organized analytical assessments regarding policy roadmap for emerging Information Communication Technology (ICT) solutions and technologies.
Prioritize the interest of Government in public sector entities under the MoITT and oversee their performance.
Create concise technology and policy briefs for the Government and thereby enabling effective decision-making.
Conceptualize, process for approval from the competent fora and subsequently monitor telecom related development projects including those funded through the Public Sector Development Program (PSDP).
Conceptualize, process for approval from the competent fora and oversee performance of major GoP initiatives/programs like bridging the digital divide through provision of ICT services in the un-served and underserved areas, proliferation of broadband services, capacity building of the telecom sector and inculcation of research and development culture in the ICT sector.
Effective liaison with telecom industry for sector development, ensuring that MoITT is kept at the forefront of technological understanding on cellular, fixed, wireless, data and broadband technologies.
Organize the Wireless Wing planning and operations within the Ministry. Monitor and interpret market developments and their implications for the sector.
Provide research and analysis in support of MoITT policy initiatives and support for consultations, speeches and position papers.
Facilitate the Ministry to issue appropriate policy directives for the telecom sector as and when required.
Analyze international telecommunications indices, rankings, and benchmarking frameworks to identify performance gaps and support the formulation of effective telecom policies and reform initiatives.
Preparation Terms of Reference (TORs), Request for Proposals (RFPs), managing competitive bidding processes, bid evaluation, and ensuring compliance with public procurement regulations.
Any other task to be assigned.
DURATION:
Appointment of the Director General (Telecom Wireless) shall initially be made on contract for three years which will be extendable for a further period of two years (year to year basis) on the recommendation of Performance Evaluation Committee in accordance with the MP Scale Policy, 2020.
DISQUALIFICATION:
No person shall be eligible for appointment as Director General (Telecom Wireless), who:
has been or is dismissed from service as a consequence of disciplinary proceedings;
has been or is convicted, by a court of competent jurisdiction, for an offence involving moral turpitude;
either at the time of appointment as Director General (Telecom Wireless) or thereafter during such appointment was not or is not a citizen of Pakistan; or
Derived benefits from the National Reconciliation Ordinance, 2007 (LX of 2007).
MANNER OF APPOINTMENT:
The appointment shall be made as per prescribed procedure of appointment against the MP-II Scale positions.
The vacancy of the Director General (Telecom Wireless) has been uploaded by the Ministry of IT and Telecom on its website and also advertised in the national leading newspapers.
A shortlisting Committee shall be constituted with the approval of Secretary, IT and Telecom, for shortlisting of applications.
The Selection Committee for appointment in the MP Scale shall recommend three most suitable candidates out of the shortlisted candidates for appointment of one of them with the approval of the Prime Minister.
PAY PACKAGE:
The Director General (Telecom Wireless) shall receive pay package of MP-II Scale in accordance with the MP Scale Policy 2020, of the Federal Government.
LEAVE:
The Director General (Telecom Wireless) shall earn leave in accordance with the MP Scale Policy 2020, of the Federal Government.
CONFLICT OF INTEREST:
The Candidates for appointment as Director General (Telecom Wireless) shall have to seek retirement from his existing Department and post or his appointment shall be subject to acceptance of resignation from designated authority and shall not, during his term of office, engage himself in any other service, business, vocation or employment which may have any direct or indirect effect on his performance as Director General (Telecom Wireless). The candidates already in the government or engaged by the government in any capacity shall have to produce NOC from their respective authority for appearing in the interviews.
DIRECTOR GENERAL (TELECOM WIRELESS) TO BE PUBLIC SERVANT:
The Director General (Telecom Wireless) appointed under these rules when acting or purporting to act in pursuance of any of the provisions of these rules shall be deemed to be a public servant within the meaning of section-21 of the Pakistan Penal Code (Act XLV of 1980).
TERMINATION OF CONTRACT:
The contract of Director General (Telecom Wireless) may be terminated on completion of tenure or by giving one month's notice on either side or payment of one month's basic pay in lieu thereof.

title: Director General (Debt)
qualifications: Bachelor of Science in Economics and Mathematics
Master of International and Development Economics (MIDEC)
MSc International Economics Banking and Finance
description:
Provide strategic leadership and overall direction to the Debt Management Office (DMO) as Head of the Office, ensuring alignment of public debt management with fiscal policy objectives, macroeconomic stability, and long-term debt sustainability.
Set and approve the strategic framework for public debt management, including the Medium-Term Debt Management Strategy (MTDS), Annual Borrowing Plan (ABP), and key policy guidelines, in compliance with the FRDL Act, 2025.
Exercise strategic oversight over domestic and external borrowing programs, including market access, funding diversification, and alignment of financing choices with cost-risk objectives.
Oversee the debt risk management framework, including strategic benchmarks for interest rate, refinancing, and contingent liability risks.
To ensure continuous improvements in borrowing policies and processes.
To ensure diversification of funding sources for the government through introduction of various domestic and external debt instruments.
Ensure a strong governance, accountability, and internal control framework across the DMO, including clear delegation, segregation of duties, and compliance with laws and policies.
Lead high-level engagement with key stakeholders, including the Finance Secretary, SBP, EAD, IMF, development partners, investors, and credit rating agencies.
Provide strategic oversight of investor relations and market communication, ensuring consistent messaging and credibility of the government’s debt management framework.
Ensure timely submission and strategic coherence of statutory debt publications and fiscal risk disclosures, including inputs to the budget and debt sustainability assessments.
Provision of leadership on debt data questions and ensure compliance with reporting requirements.
Guide institutional development and capacity building of the DMO and adoption of international best practices.
Advise the government on strategic debt-related policy matters and perform any other functions assigned by the competent authorities under the FRDL Act, 2025.
Educational Qualification:
Minimum 16 years of education / Master’s degree in Finance, Economics, or a related field from an HEC-recognized or internationally reputable institution; OR
Any one of the following professional qualifications:
o Chartered Financial Analyst (CFA) Charter-holder.
o FRM
Experience Requirement:
Minimum 17 years of Service in Officer Cadre in finance, public debt management, treasury, or financial / capital markets, of which 5 years must be in a leadership position equivalent to that of BS-20.
Skills Requirement:
Solid understanding of the interlinkages between debt management, monetary policy, cash management, and fiscal operations.
Familiarity with both market and non-market (e.g., IFIs) sources of financing and their respective terms.
Knowledge of risk-based debt management frameworks, including strategic benchmarks and risk indicators.
Practical experience with relevant IT systems and financial platforms (e.g., Bloomberg, Reuters, Excel).
Strong command of the English and Urdu languages, particularly for engagement with domestic and international stakeholders

title: Motion Design Lead / Senior Animator
qualifications: Bachelors in Information & Communication Systems Engineering (BICSE)
Bachelor of Arts - Information Technology - BA(IT)
Bs Television Broadcast and Digital Media
Bachelors of Business and Information Technology (BBIT)

description:
To develop visually engaging motion content that conveys climate challenges and policy responses in a compelling way.
To lead the creative development, execution, and quality control of all animated outputs within the ministry.
To act as the sole technical expert on motion design within the digital media team.
Demonstrate a strong sense of visual storytelling, creative concept development, and aesthetic judgment.
Develop mood boards, storyboards, and animation styles that match MoCC’s tone and climate narratives.
Ensure the design and animation reflect regional diversity, inclusivity, and are engaging to a wide audience, including youth and vulnerable communities.
Maintain a consistent visual identity across all animations, aligning with MoCC’s communication goals and cultural context. Conceptualize and produce motion graphics, animated explainers, and infographic videos aligned with MoCC’s campaigns and climate communication priorities.
Animate climate data (e.g., temperature shifts, rainfall patterns, biodiversity loss) into visual stories using charts, transitions, and maps. Translate policy material into animated sequences for public awareness.
Ensure motion content is optimized for various platforms (Reels, TikTok, YouTube Shorts, TV spots, presentations). Maintain project files, versioning, asset libraries, and rendering outputs.
Troubleshoot issues related to video rendering, compatibility, and design consistency. Work closely with the Head of Communications and policy teams to shape the visual storytelling strategy from a climate perspective.
Provide creative input during content planning meetings and communication briefings.
Recommend tools, plug-ins, or visual styles to enhance quality and impact. Manage multiple timelines and requests independently. Prioritize urgent campaigns (e.g., disaster alerts, national/international climate days).
Produce rapid-response animations when required (e.g., infodemic corrections, social media myths). Produce inclusive visuals reflecting Pakistan’s regional diversity.
Ensure bilingual (Urdu-English) execution with appropriate fonts, typography, and script flow. Design with accessibility in mind (e.g., readable text, color contrast, visual hierarchy).
Strong proficiency in:
Adobe After Effects (expressions, effects, 2.5D animation)
Illustrator, Photoshop, Premiere Pro
Optional: Blender, Cinema 4D, or other 3D tools
Demonstrated ability to translate complex or technical data into engaging motion content.
Experience producing work in or for the public, development, or environmental sectors is preferred. Familiarity with Pakistan’s climate issues and governance context is a strong asset.
A professional portfolio demonstrating range and quality in animated work is mandatory.

title: Head of Internal Audit
description:
Ensure compliance with sound internal auditing principles and best practices and seek guidance from the standards issued by international standard setting bodies.
Ensure due professional care in carrying out audit assignments and maintain integrity and objectivity.
Formulate an annual audit plan in consultation with the Audit Committee and for the purpose maintain Audit Universe covering the main auditable units and Risks Assessment Criteria for selection of audit projects in the planned activity.
Implement the annual audit plan along with any special tasks or projects entrusted by the Board of Directors through its Regulations or Resolutions, assigned by Audit Committee or requested by Chairman PNSC or considered necessary by Chief Internal Auditor himself due to exigency of circumstances.
Render reports on the audit’s findings and conclusions to the concerned departments/divisions, which shall timely respond along with details of actions taken or planned in regard to specific findings and recommendations in the internal audit communications.
Submit periodical reports to the Audit Committee summarizing results of audit activities. Also keep Chairman, PNSC and Audit Committee abreast with the important findings and recommendations of audit undertaken from time to time.
Undertake consulting services when required by Chairman, PNSC provided such services do not impair the independence of the internal audit function and functional control of the Audit Committee.
Assist in the investigation of significant suspected fraudulent activities where so required and notify the results to Chairman PNSC and Audit Committee.
Handle the documents and information given to IAD by other departments in the same prudent manner as by those employees normally accountable for them.
Make internal audit reports available to external auditors as and when demanded and inform the Audit Committee about the same.
